datasets.name: five-class artificial set
datasets.how_obtained_detail: five-class artificial data set generated by the authors (Fig. 4 p.7, Fig. 5 p.12, text p.11); sizes and dimension not printed (plotted in 2-D); no data location given

ir_definition: "Imbalance ratio or IR is computed as the proportion of the number of majority class examples to the number of minority class examples [40]. The class with maximum number of instances is the majority class and the class with minimum number of examples is the minority class."

chosen.metric: G-mean (multi-class extended G-mean) - mean Friedman rank over 20 data sets
chosen.condition: all 20 data sets, original IR, stratified 5-fold CV x 10 runs

summary_rows.label: Bonferroni-Dunn mean-rank difference vs MDO control (G-mean, C4.5, Table 3; CD = 1.2490)

outcome.stat_test: Friedman test (Iman-Davenport improved F_F) + Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc, MDO as control, q_alpha=0.05 = 2.4980, CD = 1.2490 (p.10)

win_claim.quote: MDO outperformed exiting over-sampling techniques in terms of MAUC and precision with KNN and Ripper classifiers, significantly.

uncertain: Metric choice: G-mean ranks chosen per priority, though no per-dataset G-mean table exists; values are mean ranks (lower is better), so higher_is_better=false refers to ranks (p.10)
Classifier: abstract highlights none; C4.5 taken as first reported (Tables 2-3, p.10); conclusion highlights KNN and Ripper (p.13)
source_repo per data set not stated; paper says only '20 multi-class benchmark data sets from the UCI [21] and KEEL [2] repositories' (p.8)

how_obtained='original' assumed since no preprocessing is stated; sizes/class counts of some sets (e.g., Ecoli 327/5 classes, Abalone 4,139/18 classes, Pageblocks 545/4 classes, Autos 202) may reflect repository versions or undisclosed class removal (p.9)
UKM and Contraceptive %Min printed without % sign ('9.3', '22.61'); copied as printed (p.9)

Minority/majority columns are inconsistent with the IR definition for some sets (Hayes-roth majority 'All other classes'; Letter minority 'All other classes', majority 'Class of 21'; winequality-red majority printed as just '5'); copied as printed (p.9)
n_minority/n_majority left null: not printed as counts, only class distribution (p.9)
notes: No per-dataset numbers anywhere in the paper; results only as Friedman mean ranks (Tables 2,4,6) and Bonferroni-Dunn rank differences (Tables 3,5,7) for MAUC, G-mean, precision, recall, F-measure with C4.5, KNN (K=5), Ripper (Weka). Other mean ranks MDO vs SMOTE: C4.5 MAUC 1.1750 vs 2.2250, F-measure 1.9000 vs 2.7250; KNN MAUC 1.2000 vs 2.6500, G-mean 2.1000 vs 2.4750; Ripper MAUC 1.2000 vs 2.5500, G-mean 2.1000 vs 2.7750. SMOTE applied to each minority class separately (one-vs-majority style); ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE used with OAA (p.3). Precision/recall/F-measure computed for the minority class only. Parameters: K=5 all methods, ADASYN beta=1, MDO K1=5, K2=10. Table 1 text verified against rendered page 9 image. No supplementary file referenced.
